SEO_TITLE: Why Voltage Matters in EV Charging
FACT_HOOK: It’s not just amps—voltage defines your charging speed.
FACT_EXPLANATION: Charging speed depends heavily on voltage: higher voltage allows more power transfer without excessive current, reducing heat and cable thickness. For example, Level 1 chargers run at 120V and deliver 1.4 kW, while Level 3 superchargers can exceed 800V and push 350 kW. The reason isn’t magical—it’s basic electrical engineering: Power equals voltage times current. Engineers also account for cable resistance, connector geometry, and battery acceptance rates. Some chargers dynamically adjust voltage during a session to maintain safety and efficiency, a process called constant power tapering. Batteries themselves resist high voltage differently depending on temperature, chemistry, and age, so chargers must constantly “listen” to the battery. It’s a delicate balance between physics and chemistry, yet it’s automated seamlessly for users. This explains why two identical chargers can perform differently depending on the car’s internal circuitry and battery state.
